finalText:
Here's the story the logs tell, start to finish.

Redis went down at 2:14:07am. Connection refused, right at 10.0.0.12:6379.

The app tried to cope. It switched to reading straight from the store instead of the cache. But that store couldn't take the extra load.

From there it was a slow spiral. Cache misses kept piling up. Requests kept timing out. The queue of waiting requests grew and grew, past its safe limit of 500 by around 2:29am.

Meanwhile redis kept refusing to reconnect. Attempt after attempt failed, roughly every two minutes, all the way to at least attempt 12 at 2:31am. It never came back.

The backlog finally broke things. At 2:31:44am, worker-2 ran out of memory and crashed. Eight seconds later, the whole api gave up too. The supervisor killed everything at 2:31:52am.

**Root cause:** Redis at 10.0.0.12 dropped and stayed down. The fallback to direct reads wasn't built to handle real traffic, so the backlog just kept growing until something snapped.

**Worth checking:** why redis went down and stayed down for 17+ minutes, and whether the fallback path needs a circuit breaker instead of letting the queue grow unbounded.
